ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, arts. 3-4 (UBO definition; 25% ownership threshold and control test), 9 (identification duties), 14 (PEP rules), 25 (record-keeping), 32 (suspicious transaction reporting); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, arts. 3-7; Real Decreto 95/2018, de 30 de marzo, creating the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales; Ley 14/2023, de 18 de mayo, reforming the UBO register access and filing regime applicable to all new SL incorporations; Ley 1/2010 Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) arts. 18 and 22; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on crypto-asset fund transfer traceability (USDC payment rails); Directive (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843 as transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or chamber of commerce of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Spain is party to the HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention; consular legalization required only for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder) for the incorporation signatory, bilingual Spanish/English
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; sworn Spanish translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and proof of residential address of each individual shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority / municipal registry of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy at origin, then Hague Apostille where the notary sits in a Hague jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / clean criminal record of non-resident individual shareholders (if triggered by enhanced due diligence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national police of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds declaration and bank reference letter covering the SL capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank attestation; apostille not required but must be retained by the notary and the SL for 10 years under Ley 10/2010 art. 25

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs and intended administrators against the SEPBLAC internal lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, US OFAC SDN list and UK HMT list before deed execution; PEP identification under Ley 10/2010 art. 14 for Spanish public-office holders and equivalent senior PEPs abroad; enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds verification mandatory for PEPs, nominee arrangements, shell-company structures and counterparties in FATF high-risk third jurisdictions; suspicious transaction report (comunicación de operación sospechosa) must be filed with SEPBLAC within 15 calendar days of detection; merchant payment rails intended (Stripe and USDC) require automated sanctions and name-match screening at counterparty level under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Servicio de Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social - https://www.rmc.es; applications also accepted through the Colegio de Registradores online gateway or before any Spanish notary. The RMC certificate reserves the name against identical or phonetically/semantically confusing names of existing S.L., S.A., S.A.D., S.C., C.B. and other registered entities domiciled in Spain.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SL corporate name must be written in Spanish (Castilian) and follow the orthographic rules of the Royal Spanish Academy; foreign words are admissible when transliterated in Latin script and reasonably pronounceable in Spanish; accented characters and dieresis are preserved; the name must contain at least one distinctive element and must not mislead as to the activity, seat, legal form or shareholder identity; an OEPM and EUIPO trademark clearance for the 'Commerce Scraping API' trade name is commercially recommended but is not a statutory incorporation condition.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Andalucía, Cataluña and other state or autonomous-community territorial denominations (require prior official authorization)
Banco, Caja, Caja de Ahorros, Entidad de Crédito (reserved to Banco de España / Law 10/2014 licensed credit entities)
Seguros, Reaseguros, Entidad Aseguradora (require DGSFP / Ministry licensing)
Sociedad de Valores, Valores, Bolsa, Gestora de Fondos (require CNMV licensing)
Fundación, Asociación, Colegio Profesional, Cámara (reserved to non-limited legal structures)
Real, Nacional, Gobierno, Ministerio, Administración, Estado (official or institutional character requiring prior authorization)
S.A., S.L., S.C., C.B., S.A.D., S.Coop. (legal-form suffixes reserved to the corporate type actually adopted)
Any name identical or confusingly similar to a previously reserved RMC name or registered Spanish trademark
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate is valid for 90 days and may be renewed once for an identical further 90-day period by re-filing with the RMC before expiry with applicable tariff. On formal rejection, the applicant may: (i) file a voluntary reconsideration (recurso potestativo de reposición) with the RMC director within one month of notification; (ii) appeal to the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of Madrid within two months of the rejection decision; or (iii) re-file an application listing 3-4 alternative distinctive names, which is standard market practice, thereby restarting the 90-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for the ISIC 6201 data-pipeline API activity. The SL must denominate a physical Spanish address in the incorporation deed and RMC entry; a virtual-office operator performing mail reception, legal notice service and compliance-address functions is compliant, provided the address is a real place in Spain and the operator is not a mere PO box; no local employees, premises or fixed establishment is statutorily required for a remote API/data business, but the registered office must remain effectively accessible for legal process and AEAT correspondence under art. 18 of Ley de Sociedades de Capital.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Medium: estimated 5-15% annual probability of an unannounced inspection or remote compliance verification for a small technology SL with no physical assets, inventory or cash handling; probability increases if annual invoicing exceeds EUR 2.5 million, if recurrent VAT refunds are claimed, or if the SL registers as a merchant with a payment processor requiring physical presence; AEAT, Mercantile Registry inspectors and SEPBLAC may perform documentary or on-site verifications without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 4.1, 19-22, 23, 33, 62(1), 210, 363 and 367.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry), Madrid, for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil de Madrid (Provincial Mercantile Registry) for inscription of the public deed; notarial authority for the execution and issuance of the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) recorded in the Registro Mercantil, together with Form 036 submitted to the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria for the provisional NIF.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an SL, the minimum share capital is EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,260), fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation. The capital is deposited into a temporary corporate bank account with a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by the bank's certificate of deposit attached to the public deed. There is no statutory escrow account; the funds are released on execution of the deed and are available for corporate activity immediately after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company and the adoption of its Articles of Association be hereby ratified and approved in all respects. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the statutory share capital of EUR 3,000 has been lawfully subscribed and fully paid in by the sole incorporator, and the bank certificate of deposit is accepted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office shall be fixed at Calle de Alcalá 12, Planta 4, 28014 Madrid, Spain. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the undersigned incorporator hereby appoints [Name] as sole Director of the Company, granting all necessary powers to manage the business, register the Company with tax and social security authorities, open bank accounts, and execute contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate for the Company Denomination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry), Madrid — online portal and telematic application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal application on Form RP1 to the Central Mercantile Registry requesting certification that the proposed corporate name (including 'SL' suffix) is not identical to any existing registered name. The search is performed against the Spanish company index. The certificate issued is valid for 3 months and must be annexed to the public deed.
required_dossiers: Form RP1 (aplicación de certificación de denominación)
Copy of DNI/passport of the incorporator (notarized if applicable)
Proposed corporate name with SL suffix
Proof of payment of the official certification tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected because of identical or confusing similarity, the applicant may submit successive RP1 applications using alternative names. No formal appeal is necessary; the Central Registry will issue a denied certificate, and a new application is available within the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Provisional Bank Account and Pay In the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Bank of Spain (e.g., Banco Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the future company's name with the provisional name and corporate registration pending. Deposit the minimum statutory capital of EUR 3,000 (or any higher agreed amount) and request the bank's certificate of deposit ('certificado de depósito' or 'acuñación de ingreso'). The certificate must be brought to the notary at the time of the deed.
required_dossiers: Draft deed of incorporation or draft bylaws
Negative name certificate of the company
Identity documents of all incorporators
Duly completed bank's account-opening forms and AML/KYC declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the provisional account due to pending incorporation or internal AML policies, the applicant may open an account with another institution. Alternatively, the deposit may be made through a notarial account ('cuenta de notario') or with a 'depositor' in a financial institution that supports pending-incorporation companies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary (Notaría) chosen by the incorporators, normally in Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators must appear personally before the notary, submit the negative name certificate, the bank capital certificate, and the bylaws, and sign the escritura pública de constitución. The notary will read, approve, and authenticate the deed and deliver a first copy to the company. The notary may also handle the tax form 036 and request the provisional NIF through the AEAT's telematic systems.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (original)
Bank deposit certificate (original)
Bylaws (estatutos) as approved, signed by all incorporators
Valid passport or national ID of every incorporator
Document evidencing capacity and legal representation, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary finds a legal obstacle, including a defect in the name certificate, a missing document, or incompatibility of the corporate object with law, the deed is suspended. The parties may cure by submitting an amended draft or completing the missing requirements without additional penalty; the notary must state the reasons in a refused authorization protocol.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Delegación de Madrid, Tax Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 working days of the deed date, file Form 036 with the AEAT indicating the commencement of activities and apply for a provisional NIF. The notary may also obtain it via 'cooperación notarial' immediately after the deed. The provisional NIF is used until the definitive NIF is issued after registration in the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Form 036 in triplicate, signed by the legal representative
First copy or authenticated extract of the public deed
DNI/passport of the representative
Proof of appointment as administrator (from the deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT returns the Form 036 for errors or missing attachments, the form can be corrected and resubmitted on the same day at the 'Registro Presencial' or online via the AEAT office. The provisional NIF may be granted provisionally by notifying the notary in the same notarial act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the Company in the Mercantile Registry and Publish in the Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (Commercial Registry) and BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed and Form EJ-2 in the Registro Mercantil de Madrid within the statutory one-month term. The registry qualifies the document, assigns an hoja registral, and returns the certificate of incorporation. The officers are subsequently published in the BORME; the deed's registration is declared effective from the date of filing.
required_dossiers: Primera copia (first notarial copy) of the public deed
Provisional NIF certificate issued by the AEAT
Form EJ-2 (signature specimen of administrators)
Application form set and proof of payment of the registry tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'calificación denegatoria' (negative qualification) or suspends registration, the company may file a 'recurso' with the Comisión de Calificación within two months or cure the defect by presenting a supplementary notarial act or amended deed. Upon cure, the registration is processed within 5-10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax and Social Security Registration for Definitive Operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Mercantile Registry registration, submit the definitive NIF application using Form 036 and update the census data. Register the company for corporation tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), the optional economic activity tax (IAE) if turnover exceeds thresholds, and register the company as an employer with the TGSS through the RED system, including the legal representative and any employees.
required_dossiers: Certificado de inscripción issued by the Registro Mercantil
Definitive NIF certificate
Updated Form 036/037 (declaration of fiscal residency)
TA.1 employer's Social Security registration form
Dirs account request (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is refused due to an incomplete location or missing form, an online rectification and resubmission to the AEAT is possible. For Social Security, corrections to the employer code (número patronal) may be submitted electronically within the 5-day period without affecting contribution deadlines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo / Dirección General de Industria — no industrial authorization applies to a software/data processing activity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None (statutory license not required for ISIC 6201 digital services); a municipal 'licencia de actividad' for the physical office may be required but is generally exempt for professional offices under R.D. 1008/2010

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — activity does not fall within Annexes I or II of Law 21/2013 and no physical installation is present
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no industrial discharges, VOCs, or fixed-source emissions. Waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) handling, if any, must comply with Law 7/2022, and batteries and packaging are controlled under their respective sector rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises must satisfy the general fire-safety and occupational-risk requirements of Royal Decree 486/1997 (workplaces). The municipal civil protection department conducts structural-load and fire-prevention inspections only where the rented office is located in an ordinary commercial building; no special industrial or civil-defense permit is required for an API gateway business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and its official portal at www.agenciatributaria.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by submitting an application to the AEAT, either online via the Cl@ve or certificate methods or in person at an authorized office, requiring identification documents such as passport and proof of address; the process typically takes 10-15 business days for approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not offer check-the-box elections; tax classification is determined by residency rules under the Spanish Tax Law and EU directives. Hybrid mismatch elections are available under the ATAD framework for certain cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under Facturae standard for B2B transactions; real-time VAT reporting via the SII (Immediate Supply Information) system for qualifying taxpayers; digital stamping and clearance integrated with AEAT systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT rate upon submission of customs export declaration and proof of actual export; offshore services to non-EU customers are zero-rated if the service is effectively used outside the EU and no establishment is present in Spain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ED), Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, Proof of Repatriation of Payment (Inward Remittance Certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of export zero-rating may result in penalties of up to 100% of the evaded tax, retrospective clawback of zero-rating benefits, and potential criminal prosecution under Spanish tax evasion laws.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting under the European System of Central Banks, with the Dirección General de Operaciones y Mercados overseeing reserves and payment systems; foreign exchange surveillance and statistical duties are shared with the Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional and the Comisión de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias. The Spanish Ministry of Economy is competent for capital movement restrictions under EU law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility of the euro in both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Spain's Ley 19/2003 de Régimen Jurídico de los Movimientos de Capitales y de las Transacciones Económicas con el Exterior. No exchange control authorization is required for inbound equity contributions, dividend repatriation, payments for services, or liquidation proceeds. Transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000 require ex-post statistical declaration to the Banco de España, but such filing is informational, not a prior approval. Profit remittance is unrestricted and subject only to standard withholding tax compliance and documentary bank KYC on beneficial ownership. There is no blocked capital account regime and no prioritization of current vs capital account approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in Spain or abroad, freely converted into euros, or used for treasury management. The only obligation is statistical reporting of cross-border payments and positions when thresholds apply. EU anti-money-laundering rules require full traceability of receipts, and tax law requires invoice transactions to be documented, but there is no percentage surrender quota or statutory repatriation timeline for export collections.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-High only as an ancillary rail; not a substitute for a licensed credit institution. Authorized EU/EEA Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) operating in Spain under the PSD2 and Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 may be used for low-balance operational accounts and cross-border collections, provided they hold a passportable license (e.g., to EBA register) and appoint a Spanish AML representative where required. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot offer capital escrow-taking deposit business, cannot extend credit, and client funds must be safeguarded in segregated pools; use of an unlicenced offshore EMI is prohibited and constitutes an AML/institutional red flag. The selected entity must support IBAN, SEPA, SWIFT MT103, and ideally Crypto-to-fiat on/off ramps with compliant CFATF/EBA travel-rule attestation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a Spanish SL are not legally required to be Spanish residents, but the Bank of Spain's AML circular (5/2018) requires financial institutions to verify the identity and management authority of all UBOs and directors. In practice, Tier-1 Spanish banks mandate an in-person or video-verified interview for non-resident directors when the company is opening its first account; fully remote opening is rare absent a prior banking relationship. Physical attendance of at least one director with a notarized power of attorney is normally required for initial signatory validation. Remote video onboarding may be accepted by certain banks if the director holds a valid EU passport, the SL's constitutive documents are apostilled, and the beneficial ownership structure is transparent. To avoid delay, the blueprint assumes physical presence at a Madrid or Barcelona branch for executing opening mandates and obtaining tokenized security devices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or shareholder resident outside the EU, especially in a jurisdiction featuring high-risk or non-cooperative status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passport copies, certificate of good standing, profiles on shareholders, tax residence certificates (Modelo 030/EXR), three months of business bank statements, source of wealth declaration, and a corporate organizational chart supported by a WE-02 Spanish corporate registry extract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The commercial model is cross-border scraping and API data sales, which can trigger refusal for 'unclear economic purpose' or perceived exposure to data-regulation liability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive commercial contract with a named counterparty, customer due-diligence framework, GDPR and Data Commercialization compliance material, SWIFT and wire-flow summaries, a formal Business Plan with realistic turnover projections, and proof that permitted target websites are public APIs with lawful access terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cryptocurrency terms in treasury (USDC receipts / crypto-to-fiat settlement), which banks commonly reject outright.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blockchain transaction addresses, Chainalysis/ Elliptic due-diligence reports on source-of-funds tokens, a signed AML/CFT policy covering travel-rule compliance, licensing evidence for crypto-fiat processors, and a management letter undertaking that all crypto inflows are converted to fiat only through regulated Spanish or EU exchanges.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High throughput of small-payment commercial API invoices through a single collecting account, resembling layering or invoice-laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited monthly invoices and ledgers, historic bank statements of the Spanish SL, signed terms-of-service with API users, and a designated compliance officer questionnaire plus independent AML audit report. Evidence must reconcile every invoice to a settled card/IBAN/crypto transaction without gaps.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity subscription proceeds should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's foreign bank to the SL's EUR operational account. For EU-origin wires, use SEPA CT messages with ISO 20022 purpose code 'COMC' when financing ordinary capital transfers, or 'EQUI' when handling equity-linked settlement. For non-EU wires, include the beneficiary's 22-digit ESEPA IBAN, the SL's legal name, the CIF/LEI in field 72, and a clear payment narrative such as 'SUBSCRIPCION DE PARTICIPACIONES - INVERSION EXTERIOR DIRECTA / DIRECT FOREIGN INVESTMENT'. If the amount exceeds EUR 1,000,000, the SL must file the 'Modelo DE/SI' statistical declaration to the Banco de España within one month after the transaction; the declaration is mandatory but not authorization-gated. Net capital proceeds may remain only in a demand-deposit account; they cannot be transferred to a fintech EMI without a documented business purpose. Incoming transfer verification requires simultaneous checking of sanction lists, the correct CIF tax validation, thenotarial deed certificate identifying subscriptions, and, where the investor is a company, its certified board resolution and registry certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For commercial-data supplier payments and licensing resettlement, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR counterparties and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or SEPA CT for EUR suppliers. All outbound payments must reference the underlying commercial invoice and, where necessary, attach an electronic certificate of invoice authenticity. For higher-value hardware, custom data-labor, or recurring hosting contracts, a revocable Commercial Letter of Credit (sight tenor) is available at Tier-1 banks, opened by MT700 and settled via URC/URR 522 and UCP600 with the presenting bank; this rail is recommended only for payments above EUR 250,000 or when trade terms require protected settlement. Cross-border disbursements to shell-company-like API resellers are subject to strict seller-KYC; payment orders lacking invoice evidence are blocked by Banco de España enforcement protocols. Settlement currencies accepted for disbursements are EUR, USD, GBP and CHF; any minor-currency payment not quoted by Banco de España will need a final invoice with FX conversion clause.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts (vanilla, up to 24-month tenor) with a licensed Spanish credit institution or EU investment firm under MiFID II.
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF FX forwards for operating-currency exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market currencies (e.g., BRL, MXN, CLP, COP) if the counterparty is an EU-authorized bank and the transaction is cleared/confirmed by a reputable broker.

Cross-currency swaps for long-term capital injection funding of infrastructure or large acquirer payments, permitted only with eligible BS/ECB-supervised banks and under anchor-party derivative collateral rules.
FX options (call/put) used purely for reducing cash-flow downside volatility, subject to mandatory classification as per Bank of Spain Circular 5/2018 and EMIR clearing thresholds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (cuentas anuales), directors' report and audit report when applicable, deposited at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months after fiscal year-end; filing within one month after approval; for a 31 December year-end the final deposit deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit prevents registration of subsequent corporate deeds and certificates; fines and surcharges may be imposed by the Mercantile Registry; persistent non-filing for inactive companies can lead to administrative cancellation of the registry folio, but not automatic strike-off of an active company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the end of the six-month post-year-end period; for a calendar-year taxpayer the filing window is 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment trigger recargo (5% to 20% depending on delay), late-payment interest (interés de demora), and minimum fines of EUR 200; persistent non-compliance may escalate to tax enforcement and director liability, but does not produce administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation (declaración de titularidad real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, filed with or in conjunction with the annual accounts deposit; for a calendar-year company the deadline is no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an administrative infringement under Anti-Money Laundering Law 10/2010, with fines up to EUR 60,000 and registry blocking of corporate acts; no automatic administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is mandatory if, for two consecutive tax years, the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total assets above EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average headcount above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared under Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable); consolidated accounts of listed groups must follow IFRS-EU; Spanish GAAP is aligned with EU accounting directives.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers in an SL require notarial execution and entry in the shareholder register before legal effect; any transfer of shares during the compliance year must be reflected in the annual beneficial ownership confirmation filed with the Mercantile Registry. The confirmation identifies every individual ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% of the capital or voting rights.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (libro de inventario y cuentas anuales)
Register of Share Transfers and Encumbrances

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - USD 1,200 per annum for a registered office and corporate secretarial agent in Spain
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800 - USD 7,000 for a certified audit of a small or medium-sized SL

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for a Spanish-resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL). The general rate may not apply to qualifying new entities, microenterprises, small enterprises, or other specially regulated taxpayers.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created entities carrying on a genuine economic activity generally apply 15% in the first tax period in which the taxable base is positive and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. For tax periods beginning in 2025, qualifying microenterprises with net turnover below EUR 1 million generally apply 17% to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable base and 20% to the remainder; qualifying small enterprises with net turnover below EUR 10 million generally apply 20%. Eligibility, transition rules, group turnover and excluded-entity rules must be checked for the relevant tax period. Statutory incentives may include R&D and technological innovation tax credits, patent-box relief, employment-related incentives and deductions for certain investments; availability depends on statutory conditions and documentation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward; Spanish tax losses do not expire after five years. Their use is generally subject to a 70% taxable-base limitation, with a EUR 1 million minimum offset and additional turnover-based restrictions for larger taxpayers, subject to statutory exceptions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) e-Office using an accepted electronic certificate. Modelo 202 is used for advance corporate tax payments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 200: annual. Modelo 202: generally three advance-payment installments annually, in April, October and December, if applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200: within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax period ends; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally 1–25 July. Modelo 202: generally 1–20 April, October and December. If the final day is not a business day, the applicable filing and payment rules may extend the deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), tax period dates, registered address and applicable corporate tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not change the SL's resident corporate-tax filing status. Use the SL's Spanish NIF and registered details; disclose foreign ownership and relevant related parties where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State entity form, activity and accounting information; reconcile the filed return with approved annual accounts and the accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Spanish SL's own accounts and Spanish tax position, not the foreign shareholder's consolidated accounts, except where a specific group or related-party disclosure requires information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to the tax base, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation differences, provisions, participation exemptions and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish domestic rules to income and expenses attributable to the SL. Do not deduct shareholder or foreign affiliate charges without evidence of business purpose, benefit and arm's-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose available tax losses and the amount used, subject to the applicable annual utilization limits and supporting schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain loss-year, amount and utilization records. A change of ownership or dormant/shell-company circumstances may restrict use under anti-trafficking rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate, credits and tax payable fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the rate legally available for the tax period; claim only substantiated deductions, credits and incentives; calculate tax due after permitted offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign ownership alone does not confer a reduced rate or treaty exemption. Retain evidence supporting any incentive, credit or exemption claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report related-party transactions and required information consistently with the Spanish transfer-pricing rules and applicable return schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify cross-border transactions with shareholders, group companies and other related parties, including services, software, data, IP, financing and cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the payment or refund position and provide required payment or bank details; submit the return even where no tax is payable if filing is required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder should not substitute its bank or tax details for the SL's. Confirm that any refund account is accepted under AEAT procedures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A late return filed without prior tax-authority notice generally attracts a fixed surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each full month of delay; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15%, plus late-payment interest from the statutory point. A return filed after an AEAT requirement may incur a tax penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on the conduct and aggravating factors. Late or unpaid tax may also attract statutory surcharges and interest. Separate fixed penalties can apply to information-return, bookkeeping and invoicing breaches.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable double-tax treaty relief. Qualifying EU parent companies may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring a qualifying participation and satisfaction of holding-period, beneficial-owner, anti-abuse and other statutory conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, provide the Spanish payer with a valid tax-residence certificate issued by the competent authority in the recipient's jurisdiction and any required beneficial-ownership, participation and treaty-entitlement evidence. The payer applies the lower treaty rate or exemption only where the requirements are met and retains documentation for withholding and reporting. If the full domestic rate was withheld, the recipient may seek a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure and supporting certificate and payment evidence. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and income classification; principal-purpose and other anti-abuse rules apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish withholding is generally 19% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents, subject to statutory exemptions, including qualifying EU-related exemptions where conditions are satisfied, and to applicable treaty limits. Rates differ by treaty, recipient status, beneficial ownership and characterization of the payment. Software, data access, scraping/API access and related payments require fact-specific classification as services, royalties or other income; contractual labels alone are not determinative.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish related-party transactions are generally subject to the arm's-length principle. Simplified Local File documentation is generally required where aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 at market value with the same related person or entity during the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and documentation rules. A Master File is generally required for groups with net turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to applicable rules and exemptions. Additional documentation and information-return obligations may apply independently of these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a general standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Spanish substance, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, permanent-establishment, controlled-foreign-company and transfer-pricing rules remain relevant. An SL conducting public commercial web scraping and proxy/API gateway activities should substantiate personnel, decision-making, assets, data rights, contractual functions, cybersecurity controls, customer location and the allocation of value-creating functions. Lack of substance may undermine treaty benefits, deductions, residence positions or transaction pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion, false returns or concealed income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, maintaining undisclosed accounts or deliberately misstating the tax base or withholding obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties are generally 50%–150% of the unpaid amount, depending on the infringement and aggravating factors, in addition to tax, interest and possible criminal prosecution. Tax fraud exceeding the statutory criminal threshold, generally EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period, may constitute a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine generally linked to the defrauded amount; aggravated cases can carry higher sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or administrative liability where statutory conditions are met, including for culpable failure to ensure compliance or non-payment during dissolution. Criminal liability may attach to directors who participate in or direct the offence. Imprisonment is not automatic; travel restrictions require a competent authority's order and legal basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party services, IP, data, financing or cost allocations outside the arm's-length range; failing to substantiate benefits or comparables; or omitting required documentation or disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income and assess additional tax and interest. Transfer-pricing documentation and reporting failures can attract statutory fixed or value-based penalties; the amount depends on the specific breach, adjustment and applicable penalty provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for serious or repeated compliance failures where statutory requirements are met. Personal criminal exposure requires participation in conduct satisfying the applicable offence elements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial residence, shell arrangements or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming treaty or EU relief through a conduit lacking beneficial ownership or commercial purpose, concealing the place of effective management, or routing income through entities without genuine functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Relief may be denied, withholding tax and corporate tax reassessed, and interest and applicable penalties imposed. Criminal consequences require conduct meeting the elements and thresholds of a criminal tax offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil, administrative or criminal liability depending on their role and the statutory basis. Shareholder status alone does not establish personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful web scraping, data protection or intellectual-property infringement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accessing systems without authorization, circumventing technical controls, violating contractual or database rights, misusing personal data, or reselling data in breach of applicable law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include contractual damages, civil injunctions, intellectual-property remedies, data-protection administrative fines and, where criminal elements are met, criminal sanctions. GDPR administrative fines may reach EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, for specified infringements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SL is generally liable for corporate conduct, but directors may incur personal liability for their own unlawful acts, statutory duties or criminal participation. GDPR fines are imposed on the controller or processor, not automatically on individual directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, sanctions or cryptocurrency payment-control failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using USDC or other payment rails to conceal beneficial ownership, evade sanctions, facilitate illicit funds, or ignore applicable customer due diligence, reporting or recordkeeping obligations where the SL is a regulated obliged entity or otherwise subject to the relevant rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences depend on the applicable AML, sanctions and payment-services regime and may include administrative fines, asset freezes, authorization consequences and criminal penalties. A software/API business is not automatically an AML-obliged entity solely because it accepts cryptocurrency; its activities and regulatory status must be assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal administrative or criminal liability for their own participation, consent, negligence where prescribed by law, or breach of specific supervisory duties. Personal travel restrictions and imprisonment require an applicable legal order or criminal judgment.
